body.subject: Uniformed contingents parading with the Jalur Gemilang at the 59th Merdeka Day celebrations
body.alt: Rows of uniformed officers marching in formation while carrying the red, white, blue and yellow Jalur Gemilang and other flags during a Merdeka Day parade.

body.subject: Celebrants waving the Jalur Gemilang during national day festivities in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah
body.alt: A smiling crowd in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, proudly raising and waving the Malaysian national flag during an open-air national day celebration in East Malaysia.

hero.subject: The Petronas Twin Towers rise above the Kuala Lumpur skyline, the emblem of Malaysia's modernisation drive.
hero.alt: The gleaming Petronas Twin Towers soar above the Kuala Lumpur skyline under a bright sky.

body.subject: The fountain at KLCC Park, in the Kuala Lumpur City Centre
body.alt: Jets of water arc from the Symphony Lake fountain in KLCC Park, framed by manicured green lawns and landscaped city greenery beneath a bright tropical sky.

body.subject: The Merdeka 118 tower, one of the world's tallest buildings, in Kuala Lumpur
body.alt: The slender, diamond-faceted Merdeka 118 skyscraper tapers to a tall spire high above the Kuala Lumpur skyline, one of the tallest buildings in the world.

hero.subject: The Johor-Singapore Causeway, the physical land link across the Straits of Johor connecting Malaysia and Singapore, which separated from Malaysia in 1965.
hero.alt: The Johor-Singapore Causeway stretches low across the shimmering Straits of Johor, carrying road and rail toward the Singapore shoreline on the horizon as seen from the Malaysian side.

hero.subject: Bangunan Parlimen in Kuala Lumpur, the Parliament House of Malaysia, embodying the constitutional order the Reid Commission's 1957 constitution created.
hero.alt: Malaysia's Parliament House stands in landscaped grounds in Kuala Lumpur, its slender office tower and sculptural ribbed legislative chamber gleaming in bright daylight.

hero.subject: The federal government precinct at Putrajaya, with the rose-domed Putra Mosque and the Perdana Putra complex, representing national development.
hero.alt: The pink-domed Putra Mosque and the grand Perdana Putra administrative complex overlook a calm lake in Putrajaya, Malaysia's purpose-built federal capital.

body.subject: The Seri Wawasan Bridge over Putrajaya Lake, in the federal administrative capital
body.alt: The white, sail-shaped pylon of the cable-stayed Seri Wawasan Bridge rises over the calm waters of Putrajaya Lake, steel cables fanning out to its deck.

body.subject: Putra Bridge (Jambatan Putra) over Putrajaya Lake, in the federal administrative capital
body.alt: The Isfahan-inspired Putra Bridge arches across Putrajaya Lake, its tiled minaret-like piers and pointed arches reflected in the water beneath a blue sky.

hero.subject: Tunku Abdul Rahman, the first Prime Minister of Malaya and Malaysia, who led the country to independence in 1957 and governed until 1970.
hero.alt: Tunku Abdul Rahman in a black songkok, horn-rimmed glasses and a dark overcoat and tie, photographed in black and white before an aircraft during a 1960 visit.

hero.subject: Abdul Razak Hussein, the second Prime Minister of Malaysia (1970-1976) and architect of the New Economic Policy.
hero.alt: Abdul Razak Hussein in a black songkok and dark suit with a patterned blue tie, facing forward in a formal official portrait against a gold brocade curtain.

hero.subject: Mahathir Mohamad, Malaysia's fourth and seventh Prime Minister, in an official portrait during his 2018 term in office.
hero.alt: Silver-haired Mahathir Mohamad smiles warmly in a grey suit bearing a 'Mahathir' name tag before an intricately carved wooden screen.

hero.subject: Abdullah Ahmad Badawi, Malaysia's fifth Prime Minister, photographed at the World Economic Forum in 2007.
hero.alt: A composed Abdullah Ahmad Badawi in a dark suit and open-collared shirt gazes thoughtfully upward while seated before a World Economic Forum backdrop.

hero.subject: Najib Razak, Malaysia's sixth Prime Minister, speaking during a World Economic Forum session in 2013.
hero.alt: Najib Razak gestures mid-sentence in a dark suit and red patterned tie, seated against a softly lit blue 'Forum' backdrop.

hero.subject: Muhyiddin Yassin, the eighth Prime Minister of Malaysia (2020-2021).
hero.alt: Grey-haired Muhyiddin Yassin in rimless glasses and a dark suit with a Malaysian emblem lapel pin speaks into a microphone against a blue backdrop.

hero.subject: Anwar Ibrahim, the tenth and current Prime Minister of Malaysia (2022-present).
hero.alt: Anwar Ibrahim in a dark suit and blue tie faces the camera in an upper-body portrait taken at an official state visit.

hero.credit: U.S. Department of State / Wikimedia Commons
hero.subject: Ismail Sabri Yaakob, the ninth Prime Minister of Malaysia (2021-2022).
hero.alt: Ismail Sabri Yaakob, grey-haired and wearing rimless glasses and a dark suit, in a close head-and-shoulders portrait at an official reception.

hero.subject: A brass band leads residents in a public parade in September 1945 marking the end of the Japanese occupation.
hero.alt: A military brass band leads a crowd of civilians marching along a street during a 1945 parade marking the end of Japanese rule.

hero.subject: Soldiers return to camp in Pahang after a jungle patrol during the Malayan Emergency (1948-1960).
hero.alt: A file of uniformed soldiers wades back through a flooded paddy field toward camp after a jungle patrol.

hero.subject: The memorial at Dhoby Ghaut Green commemorating the victims of the 1963-66 Indonesia-Malaysia Confrontation (Konfrontasi).
hero.alt: A stone memorial set in a landscaped urban green space commemorating those killed in the Indonesia-Malaysia Confrontation.

hero.subject: Tugu Negara, Malaysia's National Monument in Kuala Lumpur, commemorating those who died in the nation's struggle for freedom, including against the communist insurgencies.
hero.alt: The bronze Tugu Negara National Monument in Kuala Lumpur, a group of soldier figures raising a flag, standing against an open sky.

hero.subject: A calm street view of Lahad Datu town on the east coast of Sabah, the district at the centre of the Sulu claim and the 2013 incursion.
hero.alt: A roundabout and low buildings in the town centre of Lahad Datu, Sabah, under a bright sky.

hero.subject: Ibrahim Yaacob, founder of the pre-war Malay nationalist movement Kesatuan Melayu Muda and a leading figure in the rise of Malay political nationalism in the 1930s and 1940s.

body.subject: The ornamental Petaling Street gateway in Kuala Lumpur's Chinatown

body.subject: The golden Lord Murugan statue and rainbow stairway at Batu Caves, Selangor
body.alt: A towering gold statue of Lord Murugan stands beside a steep flight of brightly coloured steps climbing a jungle-clad limestone cliff as visitors ascend.

body.subject: Lowland rice paddies at Sekinchan, Selangor (Peninsular Malaysia)
body.alt: A flat expanse of vivid green rice paddies stretches to a low tree-lined horizon under a wide pale-blue sky.

body.subject: The Kinabatangan River at Sukau, Sabah (Bornean Malaysia)
body.alt: A broad, muddy brown rainforest river curves between dense jungle banks, with small green wooden boats moored at a timber jetty.

hero.subject: The Kuala Lumpur skyline at night, with the Petronas Twin Towers and other high-rise buildings of Malaysia's capital city.
hero.alt: The illuminated Kuala Lumpur skyline at night, dominated by the Petronas Twin Towers and surrounding skyscrapers.

body.subject: The Jalan Alor night hawker-food street, Kuala Lumpur
body.alt: A busy night-market food street glows under red paper lanterns as diners fill red plastic tables beside hawker stalls and a durian cart.

body.subject: Rainforest hills of Taman Negara seen from Bukit Terisek, Pahang

hero.subject: The Sarawak State Legislative Assembly building (Dewan Undangan Negeri Sarawak), with its distinctive umbrella-shaped roof, in Kuching — a symbol of the Borneo state's autonomy under the Malaysia Agreement 1963.
hero.alt: The Sarawak State Legislative Assembly building in Kuching, topped by a tall golden umbrella-shaped roof, beside the Sarawak River.

body.subject: The Sabah State Legislative Assembly building in Kota Kinabalu
body.alt: The modern tiered tower of the Sabah State Legislative Assembly building in Kota Kinabalu, the seat of Sabah's elected state lawmakers.

body.alt: The blue-and-gold-domed Kota Kinabalu City Mosque mirrored in the still waters of its surrounding man-made lagoon in the Sabah state capital.

body.alt: An ETS intercity train waiting at a platform of KL Sentral, the hub of KTM's intercity rail network.

body.alt: The bold red-and-white corner building of the Home Best furniture store in Kluang, Johor, its signboards reading Pusat Perabot Home Best Furniture in Malay and Chinese against a clear blue sky.
